content.levels_description: Top-down puzzle maps drawn in purple/blue pen on a grid of brick-like floor tiles. The stick-figure hero starts in one corner and must reach the little house elsewhere on the map. Each level mixes the legend pieces: shaded 'wall' blocks and hatched glass-like rooms, water pools (wavy lines) that need pushed barrels as rafts, conveyor 'dimension' arrows (>>>), trapezoid triangle-deflectors that bend fire jets, gun turrets on rails ('strings'), keys that open lasers, marbles/round bombs, and posts/pipes. Level 1 has a large water area beside the house; Level 3 has two marbles at the bottom and the house on the right; Level 4 has a central room ringed by arrow conveyors and a fortress-like enclosure with triangles; Level 5 has a big water basin filled with barrels and long pipe/fire lines. Levels carry invented place-names with a Nordic country (Norway, Sweden, Finland).

notes: Only levels 1-5 of the announced 30 are in these scans. English is the author's own child spelling (Tranangle, Mable, Laze, Rewide) — kept as written. Listed in the game index (scan0028) as 'INTELLIGENT QUALITY (*)'. Printed Vietnamese table shows through from the back (geology survey, Thủy điện Sơn La).

game: Grid maps 'VALDEPIERO' / 'RAUL FETEND' (coloured-border X-O maps)

content.summary: Top-down maps drawn cell-by-cell on squared paper in purple pen: X marks form walls/roads, O clusters, small squares, dots and a ⊗ symbol fill the blocks (no legend on these sheets). Each finished map has a header bar: a 5-letter name, a number (67-161; maybe a time limit or target), a boxed '0' icon, and one letter (in a little cube or circle). Read in order, the letters spell the two titles written on the sheets: START V, BERUH A, SIVET L, BABLO D, WONGL E, FACEN P, PURPE I, QUARE E, THAIR R, TINON O = 'VALDEPIERO'; then SEPYE R, MINBA A, ZINTE U, RINCE L, CROSS F, SPAKE E = 'RAUL FE…' of 'RAUL FETEND' (the T-E-N-D maps would be the six untitled, uncoloured grids scan0053-0058, never finished). The START sheet also has a video-game title menu ('▽ VALDEPIERO', '▷ START / PASSWORDS / EXIT'), so the letters are probably the password collected stage by stage. The names echo footballers (Del Piero, Raúl).

year_hint: c. 2002-2003 (marked '(New!)' in the game index scan0028; uses AoE II civ/scenario names)

content.title: WALL CHESS ADVENTURE
content.code_meaning: Each part is a chess puzzle/battle on a normal 8x8 board. 'W:' = where the player's White army is set up ('Random', or a zone like 'A-E1-4' = files A-E, ranks 1-4; 'PA-H6' = White pawns on A6-H6; 'QG6' = White queen on G6). 'B:' = the Black (enemy) position: K/Q/R/B/N + square (KG8 = king on g8, RC.G8 = rooks on c8 and g8); bare squares are pawns (F.G.H7 = pawns f7, g7, h7; D4.5.6 = pawns d4, d5, d6). 'Food:' = enemy pieces/squares you must capture ('0' = none, 'All' = everything). 'Mission:' = the target square to reach or take in the last part of a level (the capital). Built on his 'Cờ Wall' (wall chess) game, so wall squares were probably also placed on the board.

game: Festival Huế 2000 (creature card game)
year_hint: 2000-2001 (cards cut from Festival Huế 2000 souvenir/promo card stock)

content.physical: About 70 small cards. The backs are printed red 'FESTIVAL HUẾ 2000' cards with yellow brush strokes. Each blank white face is hand-written in pencil in three parts: NAME / ability (Vietnamese) / value in đồng (1đ-8đ). The photos show them spilled next to a 'Mực viết máy Thiên Long' fountain-pen ink box (used as the card box) and a folded paper note. scan0001 shows the faces of all 70 cards laid out in a grid.

cards.name: MANJ
cards.power: Có gai và áo giáp (has spikes and armour)

cards.name: BAB
cards.power: Có kiếm và áo giáp (has sword and armour)

cards.name: PUZZ
cards.power: Vừa bay vừa ném đá xuống (flies and drops rocks)

cards.name: TELL
cards.power: Lấy roi quật (lashes with a whip)

cards.name: Họ nhà Si
cards.power: Thu phục quân họ nhà Si (recruits the Si family units)

cards.name: LAND
cards.power: Có kiếm rất sắc bén (has a very sharp sword)

cards.name: FiF
cards.power: Thổi mũi tên theo ý (blows arrows at will)

COSiM
cards.power: Đấm một nhát là bẹp dí (one punch flattens)

cards.name: MARi
cards.power: Có sức tự nổ rất lớn (huge self-explosion power)

cards.name: 5 vị thần sức mạnh (5 gods of strength)
Họ nhà Ba
cards.power: Thu phục quân họ nhà Ba (recruits the Ba family units)

families.Si/Số 1-6: six numbered 'Si' cards, all 'Ném đạn' (throw shot), values 6đ, 5đ, 4đ, 3đ, 2đ, 1đ for Số 1-6
families.BA/Số 1-4: four numbered 'Ba' cards, all 'Có chất độc' (poisonous), values 4đ, 3đ, 2đ, 1đ for Số 1-4
families.Họ nhà Si / Họ nhà Ba: 2đ cards that 'thu phục' (win over/recruit) every card of that family
families.Gods: Thần Lửa (fire god) 7đ, Thần Núi (mountain god) 7đ, Vị thần sức mạnh 7đ, 5 vị thần sức mạnh 8đ (highest)

content.value_distribution: 1đ x9, 2đ x12, 3đ x14, 4đ x11, 5đ x10, 6đ x10, 7đ x3, 8đ x1 (total 70 cards)
content.inferred_rules: No rule sheet survives. From the cards: the đ number is the creature's strength (or price). Players most likely draw or buy creatures and battle by comparing values, with the Vietnamese ability as a special effect: MOUSE 'chạy trốn' escapes a fight, BAS/MARI 'tự nổ' blow up together with the opponent, poison/numbing cards weaken the target, 'Phòng thủ' cards block, RANGUN 'tàng hình' (invisible) can't be targeted, and the 'Họ nhà' cards capture a whole numbered family. In the game index (scan0030) 'Festival Hue 2000' is listed as one of his own inventions (VNA).

notes: All 70 faces on scan0001 are legible; the photos (IMG_2249-2251) show the same cards (DOKA, BAS, CETTA, Si/Số 5, BIG, MARI, SMALL, YOG, NEPA, NAMAH, ZAJAZ, MAX, RANGUN, Si/Số 2, BOKK, LAND, FEE, MOUSE, DAIN, COSIM, TITOP, 5 vị thần sức mạnh...) plus their red backs. Names are made-up or English words (MOUSE, LION, BIG, SMALL, MEGA, NINJA, SUMO, MINE); 'RUỒI' (fly) and 'CON CUA' (crab) are Vietnamese animals.

content.inferred_rules: An AoE-style card battle/economy game: you pay 'Cost' to field a unit card, upgrade it by swapping for the same line's tier 2 then tier 3 card (stats and cost rise each tier), buy blacksmith-style upgrade cards (+attack/armor/HP% for a unit class), and play 'costs for you' cards as income (pay 1000-2000 to get double back). Fights probably compare Attack against Armor/Pierce armor and Ht points. No rule sheet in these scans.

notes: Grouped by the brief with the Festival Huế cards, but these are a separate deck: white paper faces with English AoE stats, not pencil Vietnamese creatures. The scans don't show their backs, so I can't tell whether they are also cut from Festival Huế 2000 stock. Names are his own spellings (Janessy = Janissary, Chebu/Chebuchet = Trebuchet, Catapact = Cataphract, Luke = Mameluke, Chunel = Chu Ko Nu, Dome = Byzantine/Cataphract-like, Gaia = Mangudai-like cav archer?). 'Kindne' is probably a misspelling of 'Kind name'. All numbers read clearly; a few corrected digits are taken as final.
